rationale: Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-028 (illustrative figures), A-1: without the Act landings would stay well above 40,000 tonnes a year (48,000 tonnes on average in 2022 to 2024), so the cap binds from 2028.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-028 (illustrative figures), A-2: landings are recorded and overages enforced at the designated sites.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-028 (illustrative figures), A-11: the ten small harbors are monitored only at scheduled hours, so some landings go unrecorded.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-028 (illustrative figures), A-15: recipients, processors and crew can organize at a cost below their stake.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-028 (illustrative figures), A-3: owners expect the bill to pass and the shares to keep their value past the 2033 review.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-028 (illustrative figures), A-28: the fall in Kallmark's exports (about a sixth of a 7% share) moves the North Basin whitefish price by more than a negligible amount.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-028 (illustrative figures), A-22: the Directorate's budget is raised by the stated 18 million marks.

Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-028 (illustrative figures), A-4: owners know the formula from the introduction of the bill, expect passage, and have idle vessels or spare capacity to land more in 2026 and 2027.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-028 (illustrative figures), A-6: costs per tonne differ materially among vessels.
Probability taken from the assumption table of handbook WE-028 (illustrative figures), A-6: transfers are not blocked for most owners by the 8% limit; shares are registered and may be sold.
